title: A Aftermath for the Radiators
premise: Rafael Amberdale, once a celebrated piano prodigy, returns to the crumbling Halloway Conservatory as a janitor, hiding in plain sight among the radiators and practice rooms where their family's story fractured decades ago. When a stranger appears at the funeral of Rafael's estranged mother knowing the family by the name 'Radiators'—a private joke from a summer nobody else remembers—Rafael is forced to confront what really happened the year they stopped playing. As demolition of the conservatory approaches, Rafael and the stranger, a young archivist named Wren, piece together letters, recordings, and memories to uncover that Rafael's mother spent her final years secretly preserving Rafael's music. The novel ends with Rafael playing one last concert in the condemned recital hall the night before the wrecking crews arrive, finally claiming both the name and the inheritance they had buried.
about_author: Jonah Kavanagh is the pen name of a former conservatory custodian who spent eleven years sweeping the halls of a dying music school before turning to fiction. Their work explores the quiet lives built in the shadows of other people's talent.

chapters.title: The Inventory
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Years after vanishing from the concert stage, Rafael mops the floors of Halloway Conservatory under an assumed surname, cataloguing unsaid things in a pocket notebook. The emotional beat is quiet avoidance: Rafael has engineered a life too small to fail at.

chapters.title: Notice of Demolition
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. A posted notice announces the conservatory will be demolished in spring. Rafael begins photographing rooms instead of cleaning them, and we learn through fragments why Hall C—the recital hall—was renamed after a scandal no one will discuss with them.

chapters.title: A Funeral in Bad Weather
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael attends their mother's funeral, standing at the back. Estranged siblings exchange polite nothing. The beat is grief without permission—Rafael mourns someone they loved and resented in equal measure.

chapters.title: The Stranger Who Knew
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. At the reception, a young woman named Wren introduces herself to the family using the word 'Radiators,' a nickname only Rafael's childhood household ever used. Rafael follows her outside; she claims their mother wrote to her for years. Shock cracks Rafael's careful invisibility.

chapters.title: Letters in a Shoebox
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren, an archivist, shows Rafael forty letters: their mother writing about 'my Radiator children' and mentioning a locked room at the conservatory. Rafael refuses to believe it. The beat is denial sharpening into hunger.

chapters.title: Hall C After Hours
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Rafael breaks into the condemned recital hall at night and finds the old radiator still warm—a maintenance quirk, or something stranger. Memory floods back: the summer of the competition, the injury, the lie. First real confrontation with the past.

chapters.title: What the Siblings Kept
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Rafael visits brother Tomas, who reveals he knew about the letters and chose silence to protect Rafael from 'going back.' Betrayal and tenderness tangle; the found-family theme deepens as Tomas admits he envied Rafael's escape.

chapters.title: Wren's Own Empty Rooms
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren confesses she never met the mother; she answered a classified ad seeking an archivist and inherited the correspondence unfinished. She needs Rafael as much as Rafael fears needing her. Mutual recognition between two people hiding from inheritance.

chapters.title: The Competition Tape
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. In the conservatory basement, Rafael finds a reel-to-reel recording labeled with their childhood name. Playing it means hearing the performance that ended everything. They play thirty seconds and stop. The beat is terror disguised as practicality.

chapters.title: Sister Maren's Version
chapters.summary: Maren's POV (Rafael's sister). Maren remembers the same summer differently: she saw their mother sabotage the opportunity out of jealousy, or so she has told herself for thirty years. Her chapter complicates every certainty and shows how each sibling inherited a different wound.

chapters.title: The Locked Practice Room
chapters.summary: Rafael and Wren's POV, alternating. Using the letters as a map, they locate the locked room behind Hall C's stage. Inside: stacked boxes of Rafael's childhood compositions, annotated in their mother's hand. Overwhelmed, Rafael flees; Wren stays and reads alone.

chapters.title: Annotations
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren catalogs the scores and discovers marginalia revealing the mother attended Rafael's secret comeback attempt years ago—and left before being seen. Grief reframes into something like forgiveness. Wren decides to finish the archive regardless of Rafael's readiness.

chapters.title: Tomas Breaks
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Confronted with the annotations, Tomas admits he was the one who told their mother about the comeback attempt, believing reunion was possible. His guilt over the outcome made him complicit in silence. The beat is confession as relief and rupture.

chapters.title: The Radiators, Reassembled
chapters.summary: Ensemble chapter. The three siblings and Wren share dinner in the condemned building's cafeteria, telling the summer's story together, versions colliding. For one evening they are a family again—imperfect, arguing, laughing. Found family crystallizes around shared memory rather than blood harmony.

chapters.title: Demolition Moved Up
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The demolition date moves up six weeks. Panic forces decision: whatever the locked room holds must be understood now. Rafael agrees to listen to the full tape—with Wren beside them. Rising tension; the clock becomes a character.

chapters.title: Side B
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. The tape's second side isn't the competition—it's their mother's own playing, recorded the night before she abandoned her career, followed by her voice explaining why she pushed Rafael so hard and why she finally let go. Rafael hears love inside the damage for the first time.

chapters.title: The Offer Rafael Refuses
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A preservation society offers to salvage the building if it can be shown to hold cultural significance. Wren urges Rafael to go public as the prodigy returned. Rafael refuses—visibility still feels like annihilation. Conflict between the two halves of the found family.

chapters.title: Maren's Reckoning
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren confronts her own fabricated memory by visiting the retired conservatory director, learning the mother's 'sabotage' was actually protection from an abusive juror. Maren must dismantle the grievance that structured her adult life. Catharsis through correction.

chapters.title: One Night Only
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. On the eve of demolition, Rafael makes the choice themselves—not for the archive, not for Wren, but because the hall deserves to hear its last sound honestly. They post a single handwritten notice: tonight, Hall C, one performance. Terror and resolve in equal measure.

chapters.title: The Last Recital
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. Rafael plays their childhood compositions in the freezing hall while the Radiators—siblings, Wren, strangers off the street—fill the seats. Midway, Rafael plays the mother's piece from Side B. The beat is transfiguration: grief performed becomes gift.

chapters.title: What the Wrecking Ball Keeps
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Dawn. The demolition crew arrives to find the hall emptied but the archive legally donated, the building's story preserved in documents and in the people who heard the concert. Rafael signs their true name on the donation form. Inheritance accepted at last.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Warm
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, coda. Months later, Wren and Rafael install the archive in a small public library; the radiator from Hall C sits restored in the reading room, still warm. Rafael teaches neighborhood kids piano badly and happily. The beat is quiet continuation: family is what you keep tending after the building falls.
